I1.quote: Excess hydrogen adsorption measurements were performed on a 330 mg Basolite Z377 pellets sample using a volumetric Sieverts’ apparatus (PCT-Pro 2000 from Hy-Energy LLC) over the 0–50 bar and 50–120 K ranges.

I2.quote: Searched for a measured majority-carbon sorbent; none found. Only Basolite Z377 (MOF-177) powder and pellets were measured, pellets 'containing less than 3 wt% of graphite as a binder'. AX-21 carbon data are from ref. 27.

I3.quote: The excess hydrogen adsorption isotherms measured on Basolite Z377 pellets over 50–120 K and up to 5 MPa are presented in Fig. 2.
I3.location: main, p. 4 (journal p. 3530), Section 4.2 and Fig. 2 (pressure axis in MPa, temperatures in legend)

I4.quote: The densified MOF-177 has a specific surface area of about 2920 m2 g−1, a value about 26% less than the powder sample, which is about 3965 m2 g−1.
I4.location: main, p. 3 (journal p. 3529), Section 4.1; Table 1, main p. 4 (journal p. 3530)

I5.quote: Exploring and evaluating on-board solid state hydrogen storage systems performance are of great interest for fuel cell electric vehicles development.
I5.location: main, p. 1 (journal p. 3527), abstract, first sentence

notes: I1, I3, I4 and I5 are met for the MOF-177 sample, which is not a carbon sorbent (MOFs are excluded by protocol section 3; the <3 wt% graphite binder is not the majority component). The AX-21 carbon comparison (35 mg g-1 at 3.5 MPa, 77 K, SSA 2000 m2 g-1, Table 1) is quoted from Chahine and Bose (ref. 27), not measured here, so I2 fails and not_carbon applies. Not retracted (is_retracted false); original research, not duplicate_data (pellet isotherms are new; only powder comparison values come from earlier work, ref. 28).
